qualitative.gate_2_reason: Speculative commodity price-taker (gold and copper mining) lacking essential Western utility; exposed to volatile global spot pricing and high geopolitical risk in developing jurisdictions.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). Upstream gold and copper mining is a speculative commodity price-taking business lacking an essential Western consumer need or entrenched daily habit. Subject to global spot price cycles (LBMA/COMEX) and heavy asset concentration in non-Western jurisdictions with elevated geopolitical and resource-nationalism risk. Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: Barrick is a pure price-taker whose realizations depend entirely on London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) and COMEX spot fixing. Gold is an unconsumable store-of-value/monetary asset rather than an everyday Western functional necessity or ritual. Upstream mining requires massive capital reinvestment (sustaining & growth capex), with multi-year returns on capital (ROIC) fluctuating wildly between 3% and 10% across the metal cycle, failing compounder thresholds. Substantial production comes from jurisdictions with high political and regulatory risk, including Mali, DRC, Zambia, and Pakistan.
